arxiv-2103-16230.title: Modelling of Interfacial Flows Based on An Explicit Volume Diffusion Concept
arxiv-2103-16230.creator: B. Wang, M. J. Cleary, A. R. MasriSchool of Aerospace, Mechanical and Mechatronic EngineeringThe University of SydneySydney 2006, NSW, Australia bosen.wang@sydney.edu.au
arxiv-2103-16230.description: Abstract A novel volume of fluid model (VoF) called explicit volume diffusion (EVD) is developed for the simulation of interfacial flows, including those with turbulence and primary spray atomisation. The EVD model is derived by volume averaging the VoF equations over a physically-defined length scale. This introduces unclosed sub-volume flux, sub-volume stress and volume averaged surface tension force.

arxiv-2208-08174.title: SOFIA FEEDBACK survey: PDR diagnostics of stellar feedback in different regions of RCW 49
arxiv-2208-08174.creator: M. Tiwari, M. Wolfire, M. W. Pound, E. Tarantino, R. Karim, L. Bonne, C. Buchbender, R. Güsten, C. Guevara, S. Kabanovic, Ü. Kavak, M. Mertens, N. Schneider, R. Simon, J. Stutzki, A. G. G. M. Tielens
arxiv-2208-08174.description: Abstract We quantified the effects of stellar feedback in RCW 49 by determining the physical conditions in different regions using the [C II ] 158 μ \mu m and [O I ] 63 μ \mu m observations from SOFIA, the 12 CO (3-2) observations from APEX and the H 2 line observations from Spitzer telescopes.

arxiv-2211-01391.title: The Origin of Buckling Instability in Galactic Bars: Searching for the Scapegoat 2022 The Origin of Buckling Instability in Galactic Bars: Searching for the Scapegoat – A
arxiv-2211-01391.creator: Xingchen Li, Isaac Shlosman, Daniel Pfenniger, Clayton Heller
arxiv-2211-01391.description: Abstract The buckling process in stellar bars is full of ambiguities and unsolved issues. We analyze the origin of the buckling instability in stellar bars by means of high-resolution N N -body simulations. Previous studies have promoted the nonresonant firehose instability to be responsible for the vertical buckling.

arxiv-2502-06191.title: Wearable AR in Everyday Contexts: Insights from a Digital Ethnography of YouTube Videos 3192 Conference: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems; April 26-May 1, 2025; Yokohama, Japan CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI ’25), April 26-May 1, 2025, Yokohama, Japan D
arxiv-2502-06191.creator: Tram Thi Minh Tran, Shane Brown, Oliver Weidlich, Soojeong Yoo, Callum Parker
arxiv-2502-06191.description: Abstract . With growing investment in consumer augmented reality (AR) headsets and glasses, wearable AR is moving from niche applications to everyday use. However, current research primarily examines AR in controlled settings, offering limited insights into its use in real-world daily life.

arxiv-2502-07123.title: A nested MLMC framework for efficient simulations on FPGAs
arxiv-2502-07123.creator: Irina-Beatrice Haas, Michael B. Giles
arxiv-2502-07123.description: Abstract Multilevel Monte Carlo (MLMC) reduces the total computational cost of financial option pricing by combining SDE approximations with multiple resolutions. This paper explores a further avenue for reducing cost and improving power efficiency through the use of low precision calculations on configurable hardware devices such as Field-Programmable Gate Arrays (FPGAs).

arxiv-2504-06500.title: Data-driven Fuzzy Control for Time-Optimal Aggressive Trajectory Following
arxiv-2504-06500.creator: August Phelps, Juan Augusto Paredes Salazar, Ankit Goel
arxiv-2504-06500.description: Abstract Optimal trajectories that minimize a user-defined cost function in dynamic systems require the solution of a two-point boundary value problem. The optimization process yields an optimal control sequence that depends on the initial conditions and system parameters. However, the optimal sequence may result in undesirable behavior if the system’s initial conditions and parameters are erroneous.

arxiv-2505-23948.title: Extremal couplings, graviton exchange, and gluon scattering in AdS
arxiv-2505-23948.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by . Extremal cubic couplings in AdS relate bulk fields such that Δ i + Δ j = Δ k \Delta_{i}+\Delta_{j}=\Delta_{k} . Such couplings lead to divergent 3-point Witten diagrams, and do not occur in theories with maximal supersymmetry. We consider the simplest theories where such coupling are non-zero, which is type IIB string theory with N N D3 branes probing various configurations of sevenbranes, which are dual to certain 4d 𝒩 = 2 \mathcal{N}=2 SCFTs.

arxiv-2506-22131.title: Stationary quasi-periodic pulsations in 20-second cadence TESS flares
arxiv-2506-22131.creator: Aadish Joshi, Tom Van Doorsselaere, Daye Lim, Dario J. Fritzewski
arxiv-2506-22131.description: Abstract Context. Quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs) are an inherent feature of solar and stellar flares. However, the mechanism behind them is debated hence it is necessary to further study them to obtain a complete picture of flares and their contribution to coronal heating. Aims.

arxiv-2509-11769.title: Bose-Einstein condensates in a spin-twisted harmonic trap
arxiv-2509-11769.creator: Huaxin He, Fengtao Pang, Xianchao Zhang, Yongping Zhang, Chunlei Qu
arxiv-2509-11769.description: Abstract We investigate the ground-state phases and spin-scissors dynamics of binary Bose–Einstein condensates confined in a twisted two-dimensional harmonic trap. The ground state hosts three distinct phases—phase-separated, polarized, and phase-mixed—determined by the Rabi coupling, interaction ratio G G (between inter-component and intra-component interactions), and spin-twisting which induces edge-localized polarization through position-dependent detuning.

arxiv-2512-10670.title: Pulsed learning for quantum data re-uploading models
arxiv-2512-10670.creator: Ignacio B. Acedo, Pablo Rodriguez-Grasa, Pablo Garcia-Azorin, Javier Gonzalez-Conde
arxiv-2512-10670.description: Abstract While Quantum Machine Learning (QML) holds great potential, its practical realization on Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) hardware has been hindered by the limitations of variational quantum circuits (VQCs). Recent evidence suggests that VQCs suffer from severe trainability and noise-related issues, leading to growing skepticism about their long-term viability.

pmc-10641168.creator: Lina Guo, Mengyv Zhang, Genoosha Namassevayam, Miao Wei, Gege Zhang, Yv He, Yuanli Guo, Yanjin Liu

However, up to 80% of strokes can be prevented by modifying risk factors.ObjectiveThe study aims to assess the effectiveness of the Health Ecology Model and Self-Determination Theory (HEM-SDT) based health management intervention among individuals at high risk of stroke.

pmc-11428742.title: COVID-19 Inflammatory Syndrome: Lessons from TNFRI and CRP about the Risk of Death in Severe Disease
pmc-11428742.creator: Thaís Soares Farnesi-de-Assunção, Ana Carolina de Morais Oliveira-Scussel, Wellington Francisco Rodrigues, Beatriz Sodré Matos, Djalma Alexandre Alves da Silva, Leonardo Eurípedes de Andrade e Silva, Fabiano Vilela Mundim, Fernanda Rodrigues Helmo, Anna Victória Bernardes e Borges, Chamberttan Souza

Soluble mediators from the TNF superfamily, their correlation with clinical outcome, and the use of TNF receptors as a potent predictor for clinical outcome were evaluated.

pmc-11521690.title: Algal pigments: Therapeutic potential and food applications
pmc-11521690.creator: Ayesha Saddiqa, Zargham Faisal, Noor Akram, Muhammad Afzaal, Farhan Saeed, Aftab Ahmed, Abeer Almudaihim, Muhammad Touqeer, Faiyaz Ahmed, Aasma Asghar, Mubarra Saeed, Gebremichael Gebremedhin Hailu
pmc-11521690.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Algae‐derived natural compounds have shown significant potential in treating various health conditions, including cancer, obesity, diabetes, and inflammation. Recent advancements in nanotechnology have enabled the development of precise drug delivery systems and diagnostic tools utilizing these compounds. Central to this innovation are the vibrant pigments found in algae chlorophylls, carotenoids, and phycobiliproteins which not only impart color but also possess notable nutritional, medicinal, and antioxidant properties. These pigments are extensively used in supplements and the food industry for their health benefits.

pmc-11714087.title: Chalcone derivate as a promising candidate for treating Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-11714087.creator: Murillo Orsatto Haas, Thaís C Ruaro, Grace Gosmann, Aline R. Zimmer
pmc-11714087.description: BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive and multifactorial neurodegenerative disease that still has no cure. Different pathological processes contribute to the disease’s development, such as the presence of amyloid beta (Aβ) plaques, neurofibrillary tangles (NFTs), glutamatergic excitotoxicity, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammation1.

pmc-12404444.title: Effectiveness of Peer-assisted learning in medical education: A meta-analysis study
pmc-12404444.creator: Zhuoyang Li, Quan Wang, Junsong Wu
pmc-12404444.description: The objective of this meta-analysis was to compare the effects of peer-assisted learning (PAL) and traditional teaching methods on the theoretical knowledge and practical skill education in clinical medicine by summarizing the relevant randomized controlled trial (RCT) studies reported to date.

pmc-12427788.title: Regulatory mechanisms of Th9 cell differentiation
pmc-12427788.creator: Xingyue Liu, Ya Li, Wenwen Wu, Han Huang, Yanmei Hao, Chuanwang Song
pmc-12427788.description: Th9 cells, a distinct subset of T helper cells, are defined by their production of IL-9. Th9 cells play a role in the development of various diseases by participating in mucosal immune responses, defending tissue barriers, and regulating inflammatory responses. For instance, Th9 cells contribute to inflammatory bowel disease by secreting IL-9, which damages the intestinal epithelial barrier.

pmc-12873550.title: Food vendor characteristics in and around junior high schools and the relationship with adolescent diet quality in Ghana
pmc-12873550.creator: Elise C Reynolds, Christiana Nsiah-Asamoah, Harriet Okronipa, Charles D Arnold, Amos Laar, Christine P Stewart
pmc-12873550.description: Objective:Aspects of the school food environment can influence food purchasing and consumption among adolescents, particularly those without access to a school meal programme. Our objective was to describe and compare food vendors of junior high schools (JHS) in Ghana.Design:We conducted structured observations of food vendors within a 0·25-km radius of eight JHSs.

pmc-13241314.title: All-optical polarization control in time-varying low-index films via plasma symmetry breaking
pmc-13241314.creator: Wallace Jaffray, Sven Stengel, Alexandra Boltasseva, Vladimir M Shalaev, Maria Antonietta Vincenti, Domenico de Ceglia, Michael Scalora, Carlo Rizza, Marcello Ferrera
pmc-13241314.description: Controlling the polarization state of light with sub-picosecond speed and sub-wavelength precision remains a key challenge for next-generation nanophotonic devices. Conventional methods, such as birefringent crystals, liquid crystals or electro-optic Pockels cells are limited in speed, compactness and energy consumption.

pmc-13376759.title: Controlled human malaria infection in adults identify combinations of merozoite antigens associated with clinical immunity
pmc-13376759.creator: Rodney Ogwang, Irene N Nkumama, Kennedy Mwai, Dennis Odera, Lydia Nyamako, Kristin Fürle, Micha Rosenkranz, Rinter Kimathi, Patricia Njuguna, B Kim Lee Sim, Mainga Hamaluba, Roland Frank, CHMI-SIKA Study Team, Melissa C Kapulu, Philip Bejon, James Tuju, Faith H A Osier
pmc-13376759.description: Two vaccines are currently licensed against Plasmodium falciparum malaria but offer only partial protection that wanes, necessitating repeated dosing that is challenging to implement where it is needed most. We previously identified a subset of Kenyan adults with naturally acquired clinical immunity using controlled human malaria infection studies (CHMI, n = 86/142; ClinicalTrials.gov - NCT02739763).
